subject: octopus
title: Octopuses Learned to Use a Mirror to Find Food Behind Them

scenes.text: An octopus saw a crab ahead of it, and turned around.
At Dartmouth, three California two-spot octopuses were placed in front of a mirror.
A crab image showed up in the mirror. The real image was projected behind them.
To win a live crab, they had to ignore the reflection, turn 180 degrees and go to the right spot.
They picked the correct side about 73 percent of the time, and got faster with practice.
Turning its back was the smart move.

description:
Octopuses can use a mirror to find food that is hidden behind them.
In a Dartmouth study in Current Biology, three California two-spot octopuses learned to ignore a crab's reflection and turn 180 degrees to the real spot, getting it right about 73% of the time.
Could your pet figure out a mirror?
first_comment: Before the test, the octopuses practised with a real crab in a glass jar that they could only see in the mirror, around a 90-degree corner. Do you think an octopus is smarter than a dog?
